arabic_blocks: [342] حدثنا يحيى بن بكير قال: حدثنا الليث عن يونس عن ابن شهاب عن أنس بن مالك قال: كان أبو ذر يحدث أن رسول الله ﷺ قال: فرج عن سقف بيتي وأنا بمكة فنزل جبريل ففرج صدري ثم غسله بماء زمزم ثم جاء بطست من ذهب ممتلئ حكمة وإيمانا فأفرغه في صدري ثم أطبقه ثم أخذ بيدي فعرج بي إلى السماء الدنيا فلما جئت إلى السماء الدنيا قال جبريل لخازن السماء افتح قال من هذا قال هذا جبريل قال هل معك أحد قال: نعم معي محمد ﷺ، فقال أرسل إليه قال: نعم فلما فتح علونا السماء الدنيا فإذا رجل قاعد على يمينه أسودة وعلى يساره أسودة إذا نظر قبل يمينه ضحك وإذا نظر قبل يساره بكى، فقال مرحبا بالنبي الصالح والابن الصالح قلت لجبريل من هذا قال هذا آدم وهذه الأسودة عن يمينه وشماله نسم بنيه فأهل اليمين منهم أهل الجنة والأسودة التي عن شماله أهل النار فإذا نظر عن يمينه ضحك وإذا نظر قبل شماله بكى حتى عرج بي إلى السماء الثانية، فقال لخازنها افتح، فقال له خازنها مثل ما قال الأول ففتح قال أنس فذكر أنه وجد في السماوات آدم وإدريس وموسى وعيسى وإبراهيم صلوات الله عليهم ولم يثبت كيف منازلهم غير أنه ذكر أنه وجد آدم في السماء الدنيا وإبراهيم في السماء السادسة قال أنس فلما مر جبريل بالنبي ﷺ بإدريس قال مرحبا بالنبي الصالح والأخ الصالح فقلت: من هذا قال هذا إدريس ثم مررت بموسى، فقال مرحبا بالنبي الصالح والأخ الصالح قلت: من هذا قال هذا موسى ثم مررت بعيسى، فقال مرحبا بالأخ الصالح والنبي الصالح قلت: من هذا قال هذا عيسى ثم مررت بإبراهيم، فقال مرحبا بالنبي الصالح والابن الصالح قلت: من هذا قال هذا إبراهيم ﷺ قال ابن شهاب فأخبرني ابن حزم ان ابن عباس وأبا حبة الأنصارى كانا يقولان قال النبي ﷺ ثم عرج بي حتى ظهرت لمستوى أسمع فيه صريف الأقلام قال ابن حزم وأنس بن مالك قال النبي ﷺ ففرض الله على أمتي خمسين صلاة فرجعت بذلك حتى مررت على موسى، فقال: ما فرض الله لك على أمتك قلت: فرض خمسين صلاة قال: فارجع إلى ربك فإن أمتك لا تطيق ذلك فراجعني فوضع شطرها فرجعت إلى موسى قلت: وضع شطرها، فقال راجع ربك فإن أمتك لا تطيق فراجعت فوضع شطرها فرجعت إليه، فقال ارجع إلى ربك فإن أمتك لا تطيق ذلك فراجعته، فقال هي خمس وهي خمسون لا يبدل القول لدي فرجعت إلى موسى، فقال راجع ربك فقلت: استحييت من ربي ثم انطلق بي حتى انتهى بي إلى سدرة المنتهى وغشيها ألوان لا أدري ما هي ثم أدخلت الجنة فإذا فيها حبايل اللؤلؤ وإذا ترابها المسك
english_blocks: Yahya ibn Bukayr related to us. He said: Al-Layth related to us, from Yunus, from Ibn Shihab, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: Abu Dharr used to relate that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

The roof of my house was opened while I was in Makkah. Jibril descended, opened my chest and then washed it with Zamzam water. Then he brought a basin of gold filled with wisdom and faith, poured it into my chest and closed it. Then he took my hand and ascended with me to the lowest heaven.

When I came to the lowest heaven, Jibril said to the keeper of the heaven: “Open.” He said: “Who is this?” He said: “This is Jibril.” He said: “Is anyone with you?” He said: “Yes, Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, is with me.” He said: “Has he been sent for?” He said: “Yes.”

When he opened, we ascended into the lowest heaven. There was a man sitting with figures to his right and figures to his left. When he looked towards his right, he laughed, and when he looked towards his left, he wept. He said: “Welcome to the righteous Prophet and the righteous son.” I said to Jibril: “Who is this?” He said: “This is Adam, and these figures to his right and left are the souls of his children. Those on the right are among the people of Paradise, and the figures on his left are the people of the Fire. When he looks to his right, he laughs, and when he looks towards his left, he weeps.” Then he ascended with me to the second heaven and said to its keeper: “Open.” Its keeper said to him the same as the first had said, and he opened.

Anas said: He mentioned that he found Adam, Idris, Musa, ‘Isa and Ibrahim in the heavens—may Allah’s blessings be upon them. He did not specify their positions, except that he mentioned finding Adam in the lowest heaven and Ibrahim in the sixth heaven.

Anas said: When Jibril passed by Idris with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, he said: “Welcome to the righteous Prophet and the righteous brother.” I said: “Who is this?” He said: “This is Idris.” Then I passed by Musa, and he said: “Welcome to the righteous Prophet and the righteous brother.” I said: “Who is this?” He said: “This is Musa.” Then I passed by ‘Isa, and he said: “Welcome to the righteous brother and the righteous Prophet.” I said: “Who is this?” He said: “This is ‘Isa.” Then I passed by Ibrahim, and he said: “Welcome to the righteous Prophet and the righteous son.” I said: “Who is this?” He said: “This is Ibrahim, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.”
Ibn Shihab said: Then Ibn Hazm informed me that Ibn ‘Abbas and Abu Habbah al-Ansari used to say: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:
Then I was taken up until I reached a height where I could hear the scratching of pens.
Ibn Hazm and Anas ibn Malik said: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

Allah made fifty prayers obligatory for my community. I returned with that until I passed by Musa, who said: “What has Allah made obligatory for you upon your community?” I said: “He has made fifty prayers obligatory.” He said: “Return to your Lord, for your community cannot bear that.” So he sent me back, and He removed part of them. I returned to Musa and said: “He has removed part of them.” He said: “Go back to your Lord, for your community cannot bear it.” I went back, and He removed part of them. I returned to him, and he said: “Return to your Lord, for your community cannot bear that.” I went back to Him, and He said: “They are five and they are fifty. The word is not changed with Me.” I returned to Musa, and he said: “Go back to your Lord.” I said: “I feel ashamed before my Lord.”

Then I was taken onwards until I reached the Lote-tree of the Utmost Boundary. Colours covered it, and I do not know what they were. Then I was brought into Paradise, and there were strings of pearls in it, and its soil was musk.
entries.english_status: Personal prototype: AI-assisted working translation; two Arabic printed witnesses and two English translation families compared. Independent Arabic, English and context review pending.

notes: The selected Arabic is one report. Bewley divides its material across 342 and the first account under 343; an unnumbered Aisha account under that same 343 corresponds to selected 343. Both scopes are recorded explicitly. The Khan-family EPUB 1.8.345 has the main narrative but omits the Ibn Shihab / Ibn Hazm / Ibn Abbas and Abu Habbah attribution before the pens sentence. All selected chains and narrator transitions remain.

The selected text and modern print have فراجعني; the historical print has فراجعت. The working English retains the former as he sent me back, following the explanation in Mirqat al-Mafatih. Shatr can denote half or a part; the compared English uses half, while Fath al-Bari explicitly discusses part here. This provisional rendering uses part without supplying an arithmetic sequence or importing additional visits from other reports. Independent lexical review is required.

The selected and modern wording has حبايل اللؤلؤ, provisionally strings of pearls. The historical print instead has جنابذ اللؤلؤ. Fath al-Bari discusses both readings and competing explanations; the historical domes wording is not substituted into the selected Arabic. The Khan-family comparison also renders this differently. These are recorded variants, not reconciled descriptions.

The selected sixth heaven, order of encounters, plural blessing and change from narrated third person to first person remain. Fath al-Bari discusses differing reports; no seventh heaven or reordered encounters are imported. The historical print has additional honorifics and a shorter wording at several points. The selected form remains unchanged.

The English expands the source honorific symbols only. It does not import the comparisons’ parenthetical explanations of reward, the identity of the pens’ writers or additional place descriptions. Figures renders أسودة; souls renders نسم. These lexical choices remain provisional.

arabic_blocks: [343] حدثنا عبد الله بن يوسف قال: أخبرنا مالك عن صالح بن كيسان عن عروة بن الزبير عن عائشة أم المؤمنين قالت فرض الله الصلاة حين فرضها ركعتين ركعتين في الحضر والسفر فأقرت صلاة السفر وزيد في صلاة الحضر
english_blocks: ‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Salih ibn Kaysan, from ‘Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, from ‘A’ishah, the Mother of the Believers, who said:

When Allah first made prayer obligatory, He prescribed two rak‘ahs for each prayer, both while resident and while travelling. The travelling prayer was left as it was, and the resident prayer was increased.

arabic_blocks: [364] حدثنا يعقوب بن إبراهيم قال: حدثنا إسماعيل بن علية قال: حدثنا عبد العزيز بن صهيب عن أنس أن رسول الله ﷺ غزا خيبر فصلينا عندها صلاة الغداة بغلس فركب نبي الله ﷺ وركب أبو طلحة وأنا رديف أبي طلحة فأجرى نبي الله ﷺ في زقاق خيبر وإن ركبتي لتمس فخذ نبي الله ﷺ ثم حسر الإزار عن فخذه حتى إني أنظر إلى بياض فخذ نبي الله ﷺ فلما دخل القرية قال الله أكبر خربت خيبر إنا إذا نزلنا بساحة قوم { فساء صباح المنذرين } قالها ثلاثا قال وخرج القوم إلى أعمالهم فقالوا محمد قال عبد العزيز، وقال بعض أصحابنا والخميس يعني الجيش قال: فأصبناها عنوة فجمع السبي فجاء دحية، فقال: يا نبي الله أعطني جارية من السبي قال اذهب فخذ جارية فأخذ صفية بنت حيي فجاء رجل إلى النبي ﷺ، فقال: يا نبي الله أعطيت دحية صفية بنت حيي سيدة قريظة والنضير لا تصلح إلا لك قال ادعوه بها فجاء بها فلما نظر إليها النبي ﷺ قال: خذ جارية من السبي غيرها قال: فأعتقها النبي ﷺ وتزوجها، فقال له ثابت يا أبا حمزة ما أصدقها قال نفسها أعتقها وتزوجها حتى إذا كان بالطريق جهزتها له أم سليم فأهدتها له من الليل فأصبح النبي ﷺ عروسا، فقال من كان عنده شيء فليجئ به وبسط نطعا فجعل الرجل يجيء بالتمر وجعل الرجل يجيء بالسمن قال وأحسبه قد ذكر السويق قال: فحاسوا حيسا فكانت وليمة رسول الله ﷺ
english_blocks: Ya‘qub ibn Ibrahim related to us. He said: Isma‘il ibn ‘Ulayyah related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-‘Aziz ibn Suhayb related to us, from Anas:

That the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, attacked Khaybar. We prayed the dawn prayer near it in the darkness before daybreak. The Prophet of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, mounted, and Abu Talhah mounted, with me riding behind Abu Talhah. The Prophet of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, rode swiftly through an alley of Khaybar, and my knee was touching the thigh of the Prophet of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. Then he drew the izar away from his thigh, until I could see the whiteness of the thigh of the Prophet of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. When he entered the town, he said: “Allah is greater! Khaybar is ruined! When we descend into a people’s courtyard, then evil is the morning of those who were warned.” He said it three times.
He said: The people came out to their work and said: “Muhammad!” ‘Abd al-‘Aziz said: And some of our companions said: “And the khamis”—meaning the army.

He said: We took it by force. The captives were gathered, and Dihyah came and said: “Prophet of Allah, give me a female captive from among the captives.” He said: “Go and take a female captive.” He took Safiyyah bint Huyayy. A man came to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and said: “Prophet of Allah, you have given Dihyah Safiyyah bint Huyayy, the leading lady of Qurayzah and al-Nadir. She is fit only for you.” He said: “Call him with her.” He brought her, and when the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, looked at her, he said: “Take a female captive from among the captives other than her.” He said: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, freed her and married her. Thabit said to him: “Abu Hamzah, what did he give her as her marriage payment?” He said: “Herself. He freed her and married her.” When he was on the journey, Umm Sulaym prepared her for him and brought her to him during the night. In the morning the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was a bridegroom. He said: “Whoever has anything, let him bring it.” He spread out a leather sheet. One man would bring dates, and another would bring ghee. He said: I think he also mentioned sawiq. He said: They mixed a hays, and that was the wedding feast of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

I saw people and animals passing in front of the spear.

arabic_blocks: [370] حدثنا علي بن عبد الله قال: حدثنا سفيان قال: حدثنا أبو حازم قال سألوا سهل بن سعد من أي شيء المنبر، فقال: ما بقي بالناس أعلم مني هو من أثل الغابة عمله فلان مولى فلانة لرسول الله ﷺ وقام عليه رسول الله ﷺ حين عمل ووضع فاستقبل القبلة كبر وقام الناس خلفه فقرأ وركع وركع الناس خلفه ثم رفع رأسه ثم رجع القهقري فسجد على الأرض ثم عاد إلى المنبر ثم ركع ثم رفع رأسه ثم رجع القهقري حتى سجد بالأرض فهذا شأنه قال أبو عبد الله قال علي بن عبد الله سألني أحمد بن حنبل رحمه الله عن هذا الحديث قال: فإنما أردت أن النبي ﷺ كان أعلى من الناس فلا بأس أن يكون الإمام أعلى من الناس بهذا الحديث قال: فقلت: إن سفيان بن عيينة كان يسأل عن هذا كثيرا فلم تسمعه منه قال لا
english_blocks: ‘Ali ibn ‘Abd Allah related to us. He said: Sufyan related to us. He said: Abu Hazim related to us. He said:

They asked Sahl ibn Sa‘d what the pulpit was made of. He said: “There is no one left among the people who knows more about it than I do. It is made of tamarisk from al-Ghabah. So-and-so, the mawla of such-and-such a woman, made it for the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, stood on it when it had been made and set in place. He faced the qiblah and said ‘Allah is greater,’ and the people stood behind him. He recited and bowed, and the people bowed behind him. Then he raised his head, stepped backwards and prostrated on the ground. Then he returned to the pulpit, bowed and raised his head. Then he stepped backwards until he prostrated on the ground. That was what he did.”

Abu ‘Abd Allah said: ‘Ali ibn ‘Abd Allah said: Ahmad ibn Hanbal, may Allah have mercy on him, asked me about this hadith. He said: “I only meant that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was higher than the people. So, according to this hadith, there is no harm in the imam being higher than the people.” He said: I said: “Sufyan ibn ‘Uyaynah used to be asked about this often. Did you not hear it from him?” He said: “No.”

arabic_blocks: [371] حدثنا محمد بن عبد الرحيم قال: حدثنا يزيد بن هارون قال: أخبرنا حميد الطويل عن أنس بن مالك أن رسول الله ﷺ سقط عن فرسه فجحشت ساقه أو كتفه وآلى من نسائه شهرا فجلس في مشربة له درجتها من جذوع فأتاه أصحابه يعودونه فصلى بهم جالسا وهم قيام فلما سلم قال إنما جعل الإمام ليؤتم به فإذا كبر فكبروا وإذا ركع فاركعوا وإذا سجد فاسجدوا وإن صلى قائما فصلوا قياما ونزل لتسع وعشرين فقالوا يا رسول الله إنك آليت شهرا، فقال إن الشهر تسع وعشرون
english_blocks: Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Rahim related to us. He said: Yazid ibn Harun related to us. He said: Humayd al-Tawil informed us, from Anas ibn Malik:

That the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, fell from his horse and his lower leg or shoulder was grazed. He swore to stay away from his wives for a month and stayed in an upper room of his whose steps were made of tree trunks. His companions came to visit him. He led them in prayer while sitting, and they were standing. When he gave the salutation, he said: “The imam is appointed only to be followed. When he says ‘Allah is greater,’ say ‘Allah is greater’; when he bows, bow; when he prostrates, prostrate; and if he prays standing, pray standing.” He came down after twenty-nine days. They said: “Messenger of Allah, you swore for a month.” He said: “The month is twenty-nine days.”

english_blocks: ‘Abd Allah related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Ishaq ibn ‘Abd Allah ibn Abi Talhah, from Anas ibn Malik:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, stood, and the orphan and I stood in a row behind him, with the old woman behind us. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, led us in two rak‘ahs, then left.

arabic_blocks: [385] حدثنا نعيم قال: حدثنا ابن المبارك عن حميد الطويل عن أنس بن مالك قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ: أمرت أن أقاتل الناس حتى يقولوا: لا إله إلا الله فإذا قالوها وصلوا صلاتنا واستقبلوا قبلتنا وذبحوا ذبيحتنا فقد حرمت علينا دماؤهم وأموالهم إلا بحقها وحسابهم على الله قال ابن أبي مريم أخبرنا يحيى حدثنا حميد حدثنا أنس عن النبي ﷺ، وقال علي بن عبد الله حدثنا خالد بن الحرث قال: حدثنا حميد قال سأل ميمون بن سياه أنس بن مالك قال: يا أبا حمزة ما يحرم دم العبد وماله، فقال من شهد أن لا إله إلا الله واستقبل قبلتنا وصلى صلاتنا وأكل ذبيحتنا فهو المسلم له ما للمسلم وعليه ما على المسلم
english_blocks: Nu‘aym related to us. He said: Ibn al-Mubarak related to us, from Humayd al-Tawil, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“I have been commanded to fight the people until they say: ‘There is no god but Allah.’ When they say it, pray our prayer, face our qiblah and slaughter as we slaughter, their blood and property become forbidden to us except by their due right, and their reckoning is with Allah.”
Ibn Abi Maryam said: Yahya informed us; Humayd related to us; Anas related to us, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.
And ‘Ali ibn ‘Abd Allah said: Khalid ibn al-Harith related to us. He said: Humayd related to us. He said:

Maymun ibn Siyah asked Anas ibn Malik. He said: “Abu Hamzah, what makes a person’s blood and property inviolable?” He said: “Whoever testifies that there is no god but Allah, faces our qiblah, prays our prayer and eats what we slaughter is a Muslim. He has what a Muslim has, and owes what a Muslim owes.”

arabic_blocks: [386] حدثنا علي بن عبد الله قال: حدثنا سفيان قال: حدثنا الزهري عن عطاء بن يزيد عن أبي أيوب الأنصارى أن النبي ﷺ قال: إذا أتيتم الغائط فلا تستقبلوا القبلة ولا تستدبروها ولكن شرقوا أو غربوا قال أبو أيوب فقدمنا الشام فوجدنا مراحيض بنيت قبل القبلة فننحرف ونستغفر الله تعالى وعن الزهري عن عطاء قال: سمعت أبا أيوب عن النبي ﷺ مثله
english_blocks: ‘Ali ibn ‘Abd Allah related to us. He said: Sufyan related to us. He said: Al-Zuhri related to us, from ‘Ata’ ibn Yazid, from Abu Ayyub al-Ansari, that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“When you go to relieve yourselves, do not face the qiblah or turn your backs to it, but face east or west.” Abu Ayyub said: We came to al-Sham and found lavatories built facing the qiblah, so we would turn aside and seek the forgiveness of Allah Most High.
And from al-Zuhri, from ‘Ata’, who said: I heard Abu Ayyub, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, relate the same.

arabic_blocks: [387] حدثنا الحميدي قال: حدثنا سفيان قال: حدثنا عمرو بن دينار قال سألنا بن عمر عن رجل طاف بالبيت العمرة ولم يطف بين الصفا والمروة أيأتي امرأته، فقال قدم النبي ﷺ فطاف بالبيت سبعا وصلى خلف المقام ركعتين وطاف بين الصفا والمروة وقد كان لكم في رسول الله أسوة حسنة وسألنا جابر بن عبد الله، فقال لا يقربنها حتى يطوف بين الصفا والمروة
english_blocks: Al-Humaydi related to us. He said: Sufyan related to us. He said: ‘Amr ibn Dinar related to us. He said:

We asked Ibn ‘Umar about a man who had gone around the House for ‘umrah but had not gone between al-Safa and al-Marwah: could he have intercourse with his wife? He said: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came, went around the House seven times, prayed two rak‘ahs behind the Station, and went between al-Safa and al-Marwah. “You have had an excellent example in the Messenger of Allah.” We asked Jabir ibn ‘Abd Allah, and he said: “He must not approach her until he has gone between al-Safa and al-Marwah.”

arabic_blocks: [388] حدثنا مسدد قال: حدثنا يحيى عن سيف قال: سمعت مجاهدا قال أتي بن عمر فقيل له هذا رسول الله ﷺ دخل الكعبة، فقال ابن عمر فأقبلت والنبي ﷺ قد خرج وأجد بلالا قائما بين البابين فسألت بلالا فقلت: أصلى النبي ﷺ في الكعبة قال: نعم ركعتين بين الساريتين اللتين على يساره إذا دخلت ثم خرج فصلى في وجه الكعبة ركعتين
english_blocks: Musaddad related to us. He said: Yahya related to us, from Sayf, who said: I heard Mujahid say:

Someone came to Ibn ‘Umar and said to him: “Here is the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace; he has entered the Ka‘bah.” Ibn ‘Umar said: I came, but the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, had already come out. I found Bilal standing between the two doors. I asked Bilal: “Did the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, pray inside the Ka‘bah?” He said: “Yes, two rak‘ahs between the two pillars on the left as you enter. Then he came out and prayed two rak‘ahs facing the Ka‘bah.”

arabic_blocks: [389] حدثنا إسحاق بن نصر قال: حدثنا عبد الرزاق أخبرنا ابن جريج عن عطاء قال: سمعت ابن عباس قال لما دخل النبي ﷺ البيت دعا في نواحيه كلها ولم يصل حتى خرج منه فلما خرج ركع ركعتين في قبل الكعبة، وقال هذه القبلة
english_blocks: Ishaq ibn Nasr related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Razzaq related to us; Ibn Jurayj informed us, from ‘Ata’, who said: I heard Ibn ‘Abbas say:

When the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, entered the House, he supplicated in all its sides and did not pray until he came out of it. When he came out, he prayed two rak‘ahs in front of the Ka‘bah and said: “This is the qiblah.”

arabic_blocks: [390] حدثنا عبد الله بن رجاء قال: حدثنا إسرائيل عن أبي إسحاق عن البراء بن عازب رضى الله تعالى عنهما قال: كان رسول الله ﷺ صلى نحو بيت المقدس ستة عشر أو سبعة عشر شهرا وكان رسول الله ﷺ يحب أن يوجه إلى الكعبة فأنزل الله { قد نرى تقلب وجهك في السماء } فتوجه نحو الكعبة، وقال السفهاء من الناس وهم اليهود { ما ولاهم عن قبلتهم التي كانوا عليها قل لله المشرق والمغرب يهدي من يشاء إلى صراط مستقيم } فصلى مع النبي ﷺ رجل ثم خرج بعد ما صلى فمر على قوم من الأنصار في صلاة العصر نحو بيت المقدس، فقال هو يشهد أنه صلى مع رسول الله ﷺ وأنه توجه نحو الكعبة فتحرف القوم حتى توجهوا نحو الكعبة
english_blocks: ‘Abd Allah ibn Raja’ related to us. He said: Isra’il related to us, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Bara’ ibn ‘Azib, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, who said:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, had prayed towards Bayt al-Maqdis for sixteen or seventeen months. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, wished to be directed towards the Ka‘bah. Then Allah revealed: “We have certainly seen the turning of your face towards the sky.” He turned towards the Ka‘bah. The foolish among the people—who were the Jews—said: “What has turned them from the qiblah they had been facing? Say: To Allah belong the east and the west. He guides whom He wills to a straight path.” A man prayed with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, then went out after praying. He passed some of the Ansar in the ‘Asr prayer, facing Bayt al-Maqdis. He said that he testified that he had prayed with the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and that he had faced towards the Ka‘bah. The people turned until they faced towards the Ka‘bah.

arabic_blocks: [391] حدثنا مسلم قال: حدثنا هشام قال: حدثنا يحيى بن أبي كثير عن محمد بن عبد الرحمن عن جابر قال: كان رسول الله ﷺ يصلي على راحلته حيث توجهت فإذا أراد الفريضة نزل فاستقبل القبلة

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to pray on his mount wherever it turned. When he intended the obligatory prayer, he dismounted and faced the qiblah.

arabic_blocks: [392] حدثنا عثمان قال: حدثنا جرير عن منصور عن إبراهيم عن علقمة قال: قال عبد الله صلى النبي ﷺ قال: إبراهيم لا أدري زاد أو نقص فلما سلم قيل له يا رسول الله أحدث في الصلاة شيء قال وما ذاك قالوا صليت كذا وكذا فثنى رجليه واستقبل القبلة وسجد سجدتين ثم سلم فلما أقبل علينا بوجهه قال إنه لو حدث في الصلاة شيء لنبأتكم به ولكن إنما أنا بشر مثلكم أنسى كما تنسون فإذا نسيت فذكروني وإذا شك أحدكم في صلاته فليتحر الصواب فليتم عليه ثم ليسلم ثم يسجد سجدتين
english_blocks: ‘Uthman related to us. He said: Jarir related to us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, from ‘Alqamah, who said: ‘Abd Allah said:
The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prayed.
Ibrahim said: I do not know whether he added or omitted.

When he gave the salutation, he was asked: “Messenger of Allah, has something new happened in the prayer?” He said: “What is that?” They said: “You prayed such-and-such.” He bent his legs, faced the qiblah and performed two prostrations, then gave the salutation. When he turned his face towards us, he said: “If something new had happened in the prayer, I would have informed you of it. But I am only a human being like you; I forget as you forget. So when I forget, remind me. If any of you is uncertain in his prayer, let him seek what is correct and complete it on that basis, then give the salutation, then perform two prostrations.”

arabic_blocks: [393] حدثنا عمرو بن عون قال: حدثنا هشيم عن حميد عن أنس قال: قال عمر وافقت ربي في ثلاث فقلت: يا رسول الله لو اتخذنا من مقام إبراهيم مصلى فنزلت { واتخذوا من مقام إبراهيم مصلى } وآية الحجاب قلت: يا رسول الله لو أمرت نساءك أن يحتجبن فإنه يكلمهن البر والفاجر فنزلت آية الحجاب واجتمع نساء النبي ﷺ في الغيرة عليه فقلت لهن { عسى ربه إن طلقكن أن يبدله أزواجا خيرا منكن } فنزلت هذه الآية
english_blocks: ‘Amr ibn ‘Awn related to us. He said: Hushaym related to us, from Humayd, from Anas, who said: ‘Umar said:

I agreed with my Lord regarding three matters. I said: “Messenger of Allah, if only we took the Station of Ibrahim as a place of prayer.” Then “Take the Station of Ibrahim as a place of prayer” was revealed. And the verse of the veil: I said: “Messenger of Allah, if only you ordered your wives to veil themselves, for both the righteous and the wicked speak to them.” Then the verse of the veil was revealed. The wives of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, joined together in jealousy concerning him. I said to them: “Perhaps his Lord, if he divorces you, will give him wives better than you in your place.” Then this verse was revealed.

arabic_blocks: [397] حدثنا قتيبة قال: حدثنا إسماعيل بن جعفر عن حميد عن أنس أن النبي ﷺ رأى نخامة في القبلة فشق ذلك عليه حتى رؤي في وجهه فقام فحكه بيده، فقال إن أحدكم إذا قام في صلاته فإنه يناجي ربه أو إن ربه بينه وبين القبلة فلا يبزقن أحدكم قبل قبلته ولكن عن يساره أو تحت قدميه ثم أخذ طرف ردائه فبصق فيه ثم رد بعضه على بعض، فقال أو يفعل هكذا
english_blocks: Qutaybah related to us. He said: Isma‘il ibn Ja‘far related to us, from Humayd, from Anas:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, saw phlegm in the direction of the qiblah. It distressed him so much that it could be seen in his face. He stood and scraped it off with his hand. He said: “When one of you stands in his prayer, he is conversing privately with his Lord—or his Lord is between him and the qiblah. So none of you should spit towards his qiblah, but to his left or under his feet.” Then he took the edge of his cloak, spat into it, and folded part of it over the other. He said: “Or he should do this.”

arabic_blocks: [411] وقال إبراهيم عن عبد العزيز بن صهيب عن أنس رضى الله تعالى عنه قال أتي النبي ﷺ بمال من البحرين، فقال انثروه في المسجد وكان أكثر مال أتي به رسول الله ﷺ فخرج رسول الله ﷺ إلى الصلاة ولم يلتفت إليه فلما قضى الصلاة جاء فجلس إليه فما كان يرى أحدا إلا أعطاه إذ جاءه العباس، فقال: يا رسول الله أعطني فإني فاديت نفسي وفاديت عقيلا، فقال له رسول الله ﷺ خذ فحثا في ثوبه ثم ذهب يقله فلم يستطع، فقال: يا رسول الله مر بعضهم يرفعه إلي قال لا قال: فارفعه أنت علي قال لا فنثر منه ثم ذهب يقله، فقال: يا رسول الله مر بعضهم يرفعه علي قال لا قال: فارفعه أنت علي قال لا فنثر منه ثم احتمله فألقاه على كاهله ثم انطلق فما زال رسول الله ﷺ يتبعه بصره حتى خفي علينا عجبا من حرصه فما قام رسول الله ﷺ وثم منها درهم
english_blocks: And Ibrahim said, from ‘Abd al-‘Aziz ibn Suhayb, from Anas, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, who said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was brought wealth from Bahrayn. He said: “Spread it out in the mosque.” It was the greatest amount of wealth that had been brought to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, went out to the prayer without looking towards it. When he had finished the prayer, he came and sat beside it. There was no one he saw without giving him something.

Then al-‘Abbas came to him and said: “Messenger of Allah, give me some, for I paid the ransom for myself and paid the ransom for ‘Aqil.” The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said to him: “Take.” He scooped some into his garment, then tried to lift it but could not. He said: “Messenger of Allah, tell one of them to lift it up to me.” He said: “No.” He said: “Then lift it onto me yourself.” He said: “No.” So he poured out some of it, then tried to lift it. He said: “Messenger of Allah, tell one of them to lift it onto me.” He said: “No.” He said: “Then lift it onto me yourself.” He said: “No.” So he poured out some of it, then lifted it, placed it on his shoulders and went away.

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, kept following him with his gaze until he disappeared from our sight, astonished at his eagerness. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, did not get up while a dirham of it remained there.

arabic_blocks: [415] حدثنا سعيد بن عفير قال: حدثني الليث قال: حدثني عقيل عن ابن شهاب قال: أخبرني محمود بن الربيع الأنصارى أن عتبان بن مالك وهو من أصحاب رسول الله ﷺ ممن شهد بدرا من الأنصار أنه أتى رسول الله ﷺ، فقال: يا رسول الله قد أنكرت بصري وأنا أصلي لقومي فإذا كانت الأمطار سال الوادي الذي بيني وبينهم لم أستطع أن آتي مسجدهم فأصلي بهم ووددت يا رسول الله أنك تأتيني فتصلي في بيتي فأتخذه مصلى قال، فقال رسول الله ﷺ: سأفعل إن شاء الله قال عتبان فغدا رسول الله ﷺ وأبو بكر حين ارتفع النهار فاستأذن رسول الله ﷺ فأذنت له فلم يجلس حتى دخل البيت، ثم قال أين تحب أن أصلي من بيتك قال: فأشرت له إلى ناحية من البيت فقام رسول الله ﷺ فكبر فقمنا فصففنا فصلى ركعتين ثم سلم قال وحبسناه على خزيرة صنعناها له قال: فثاب في البيت رجال من أهل الدار ذوو عدد فاجتمعوا، فقال قائل منهم أين مالك بن الدخيشن أو بن الدخشن، فقال بعضهم ذلك منافق لا يحب الله ورسوله، فقال رسول الله ﷺ: لا تقل ذلك ألا تراه قد قال لا إله إلا الله يريد بذلك وجه الله قال الله ورسوله أعلم قال: فإنا نرى وجهه ونصيحته إلى المنافقين قال رسول الله ﷺ: فإن الله قد حرم على النار من قال لا إله إلا الله يبتغي بذلك وجه الله قال ابن شهاب ثم سألت الحصين بن محمد الأنصارى وهو أحد بني سالم وهو من سراتهم عن حديث محمود بن الربيع فصدقه بذلك
english_blocks: Sa‘id ibn ‘Ufayr related to us. He said: Al-Layth related to me. He said: ‘Uqayl related to me, from Ibn Shihab, who said: Mahmud ibn al-Rabi‘ al-Ansari informed me:

‘Itban ibn Malik, who was one of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and one of the Ansar who had witnessed Badr, came to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and said: “Messenger of Allah, my eyesight has deteriorated, and I lead my people in prayer. When the rains come, the valley between me and them flows, and I cannot reach their mosque to lead them in prayer. Messenger of Allah, I would like you to come and pray in my house so that I may take it as a place of prayer.” He said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “I will do so, if Allah wills.”

‘Itban said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and Abu Bakr came in the morning when the day had advanced. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, asked permission to enter, and I gave him permission. He did not sit down until he had entered the house. Then he said: “Where in your house would you like me to pray?” He said: I pointed out a part of the house to him. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, stood and said “Allah is greater.” We stood and formed rows. He prayed two rak‘ahs, then gave the salutation.
He said: We kept him for some khazirah that we had prepared for him. He said: A number of men from the neighbourhood came into the house and gathered.

One of them said: “Where is Malik ibn al-Dukhayshin—or Ibn al-Dukhshun?” Some of them said: “That is a hypocrite who does not love Allah and His Messenger.” The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “Do not say that. Do you not see that he has said ‘There is no god but Allah,’ desiring by that the face of Allah?” He said: “Allah and His Messenger know best.” He said: “We see his attention and his counsel directed towards the hypocrites.” The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “Allah has forbidden the Fire to anyone who says ‘There is no god but Allah,’ seeking by that the face of Allah.”
Ibn Shihab said: Then I asked al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Ansari, who was one of Banu Salim and one of their leading men, about the account of Mahmud ibn al-Rabi‘, and he confirmed it.

arabic_blocks: [418] حدثنا مسدد قال: حدثنا عبد الوارث عن أبي التياح عن أنس قال قدم النبي ﷺ المدينة فنزل أعلى المدينة في حي يقال لهم بنو عمرو بن عوف فأقام النبي ﷺ فيهم أربع عشرة ليلة ثم أرسل إلى بني النجار فجاءوا متقلدي السيوف كأني أنظر إلى النبي ﷺ على راحلته وأبو بكر ردفه وملأ بني النجار حوله حتى ألقى بفناء أبي أيوب وكان يحب أن يصلي حيث أدركته الصلاة ويصلي في مرابض الغنم وأنه أمر ببناء المسجد فأرسل إلى ملأ من بني النجار، فقال: يا بني النجار ثامنوني بحائطكم هذا قالوا لا والله لا نطلب ثمنه إلا إلى الله، فقال أنس فكان فيه ما أقول لكم قبور المشركين وفيه خرب وفيه نخل فأمر النبي ﷺ بقبور المشركين فنبشت ثم بالخرب فسويت وبالنخل فقطع فصفوا النخل قبلة المسجد وجعلوا عضادتيه الحجارة وجعلوا ينقلون الصخر وهم يرتجزون والنبي ﷺ معهم وهو يقول
اللهم لا خير إلا خير الآخرة
فاغفر للأنصار والمهاجرة
english_blocks: Musaddad related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Warith related to us, from Abu al-Tayyah, from Anas, who said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, arrived in Madinah and stayed in the upper part of Madinah among a clan called Banu ‘Amr ibn ‘Awf. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, remained among them for fourteen nights. Then he sent for Banu al-Najjar, and they came wearing their swords. It is as though I am looking at the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, on his riding camel, with Abu Bakr behind him and a gathering of Banu al-Najjar around him, until he alighted in Abu Ayyub’s courtyard. He liked to pray wherever the prayer time overtook him, and he would pray in sheepfolds.

He ordered the mosque to be built and sent for a gathering of Banu al-Najjar. He said: “Banu al-Najjar, agree with me on a price for this walled garden of yours.” They said: “No, by Allah! We seek its price only from Allah.”

Anas said: It contained what I am telling you: graves of polytheists, ruins and date palms. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, ordered the polytheists’ graves to be dug up, then the ruins to be levelled and the date palms to be cut down. They lined up the date palms at the qiblah of the mosque and made its two sides of stone. They began carrying the rocks while chanting verses. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was with them, saying:
“O Allah, there is no good except the good of the Hereafter,
so forgive the Ansar and the Emigrants.”

arabic_blocks: [425] حدثنا أبو اليمان قال: أخبرنا شعيب عن الزهري أخبرني عبيد الله بن عبد الله بن عتبة أن عائشة وعبد الله بن عباس قالا لما نزل برسول الله ﷺ طفق يطرح خميصة له على وجهه فإذا اغتم بها كشفها عن وجهه، فقال وهو كذلك لعنة الله على اليهود والنصارى اتخذوا قبور أنبيائهم مساجد يحذر ما صنعوا
english_blocks: Abu al-Yaman related to us. He said: Shu‘ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri: ‘Ubayd Allah ibn ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Utbah informed me that ‘A’ishah and ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Abbas said:

When death came upon the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, he began putting a khamisah of his over his face. When it made him feel suffocated, he uncovered his face. While in that state, he said: “Allah’s curse be upon the Jews and the Christians. They took the graves of their prophets as places of prayer.” He was warning against what they had done.

arabic_blocks: [427] حدثنا محمد بن سنان قال: حدثنا هشيم قال: حدثنا سيار هو أبو الحكم قال: حدثنا يزيد الفقير قال: حدثنا جابر بن عبد الله قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ: أعطيت خمسا لم يعطهن أحد من الأنبياء قبلي نصرت بالرعب مسيرة شهر وجعلت لي الأرض مسجدا وطهورا وأيما رجل من أمتي أدركته الصلاة فليصل وأحلت لي الغنائم وكان النبي يبعث إلى قومه خاصة وبعثت إلى الناس كافة وأعطيت الشفاعة

“I have been given five things that none of the prophets before me was given. I have been aided by fear over a distance of a month’s journey. The earth has been made for me a place of prayer and a means of purification, and whichever man of my community is overtaken by the time of prayer, let him pray. The spoils have been made lawful for me. A prophet used to be sent to his own people specifically, while I have been sent to all people. I have been given intercession.”

arabic_blocks: [428] حدثنا عبيد بن إسماعيل قال: حدثنا أبو أسامة عن هشام عن أبيه عن عائشة أن وليدة كانت سوداء لحي من العرب فأعتقوها فكانت معهم قالت فخرجت صبية لهم عليها وشاح أحمر من سيور قالت فوضعته أو وقع منها فمرت به حدياة وهو ملقى فحسبته لحما فخطفته قالت فالتمسوه فلم يجدوه قالت فاتهموني به قالت فطفقوا يفتشون حتى فتشوا قبلها قالت والله إني لقائمة معهم إذ مرت الحدياة فألقته قالت فوقع بينهم قالت فقلت: هذا الذي اتهمتموني به زعمتم وأنا منه بريئة وهو ذا هو قالت فجاءت إلى رسول الله ﷺ فأسلمت قالت عائشة فكان لها خباء في المسجد أو حفش قالت فكانت تأتيني فتحدث عندي قالت فلا تجلس عندي مجلسا إلا قالت
ويوم الوشاح من أعاجيب ربنا
ألا إنه من بلدة الكفر أنجاني
قالت عائشة فقلت لها ما شأنك لا تقعدين معي مقعدا إلا قلت: هذا قالت فحدثتني بهذا الحديث
english_blocks: ‘Ubayd ibn Isma‘il related to us. He said: Abu Usamah related to us, from Hisham, from his father, from ‘A’ishah:

A black slave woman belonged to an Arab clan. They set her free, and she stayed with them. She said: “A young girl of theirs went out wearing a red wishah made of leather strips.” She said: “She put it down, or it fell from her. A kite passed by it while it lay there, thought it was meat and snatched it.” She said: “They looked for it but did not find it.” She said: “They accused me of it.” She said: They began searching, until they even searched her private parts.

She said: “By Allah, I was standing with them when the kite passed by and dropped it.” She said: “It fell among them.” She said: “I said: ‘This is what you accused me of, as you claimed, while I am innocent of it. Here it is!’”

She said: She came to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and became a Muslim. ‘A’ishah said: She had a tent in the mosque, or a small hut. She said: She used to come to me and talk with me. She said: She never sat with me without saying:
“The day of the wishah is among the wonders of our Lord;
indeed, He rescued me from the town of unbelief.”
‘A’ishah said: I said to her: “Why is it that you never sit with me without saying this?” She said: She told me this account.

english_blocks: Qutaybah ibn Sa‘id related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-‘Aziz ibn Abi Hazim related to us, from Abu Hazim, from Sahl ibn Sa‘d, who said:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came to Fatimah’s house and did not find ‘Ali in the house. He said: “Where is your cousin?” She said: “There was something between me and him. He became angry with me and went out, and did not take his midday rest with me.”

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said to someone: “Look where he is.” He came and said: “Messenger of Allah, he is lying asleep in the mosque.” The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came while he was lying there. His cloak had fallen from his side, and dust had settled on him. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, began wiping it off him, saying: “Get up, Abu Turab. Get up, Abu Turab.”

I saw seventy of the people of the Suffah, none of whom had a cloak. They had either a waist-wrapper or a covering that they had tied around their necks. Some reached halfway down the shins, and some reached the ankles. Each would gather it in his hand, not wanting his private parts to be seen.

arabic_blocks: [444] حدثنا علي بن عبد الله قال: حدثنا سفيان عن يحيى عن عمرة عن عائشة قالت أتتها بريرة تسألها في كتابتها فقالت إن شئت أعطيت أهلك ويكون الولاء لي، وقال أهلها إن شئت أعطيتها ما بقي، وقال سفيان مرة إن شئت أعتقتها ويكون الولاء لنا فلما جاء رسول الله ﷺ ذكرته ذلك، فقال ابتاعيها فأعتقيها فإن الولاء لمن أعتق ثم قام رسول الله ﷺ على المنبر، وقال سفيان مرة فصعد رسول الله ﷺ على المنبر، فقال: ما بال أقوام يشترطون شروطا ليست في كتاب الله من اشترط شرطا ليس في كتاب الله فليس له وإن اشترط مائة مرة قال علي قال يحيى وعبد الوهاب عن يحيى عن عمرة، وقال جعفر بن عون عن يحيى قال: سمعت عمرة قالت سمعت عائشة رواه مالك عن يحيى عن عمرة أن بريرة ولم يذكر صعد المنبر
english_blocks: ‘Ali ibn ‘Abd Allah related to us. He said: Sufyan related to us, from Yahya, from ‘Amrah, from ‘A’ishah, who said:

Barirah came to her asking for help with her contract of emancipation. She said: “If you wish, I will pay your owners, and the wala’ will belong to me.” Her owners said: “If you wish, you can give her what remains.”
Sufyan once said: “If you wish, you can set her free, and the wala’ will belong to us.”

When the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came, I mentioned that to him. He said: “Buy her and set her free, for the wala’ belongs to the one who sets free.” Then the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, stood on the pulpit.
Sufyan once said: “The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, ascended the pulpit.”

He said: “What is the matter with people who stipulate conditions that are not in the Book of Allah? Whoever stipulates a condition that is not in the Book of Allah has no right to it, even if he stipulates it a hundred times.”

‘Ali said: Yahya and ‘Abd al-Wahhab said, from Yahya, from ‘Amrah. Ja‘far ibn ‘Awn said, from Yahya: “I heard ‘Amrah say: ‘I heard ‘A’ishah.’” Malik related it from Yahya, from ‘Amrah: “That Barirah…” He did not mention “ascended the pulpit.”

He asked Ibn Abi Hadrad in the mosque to repay a debt he owed him. Their voices rose until the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, heard them while he was in his house. He came out to them and drew aside the curtain of his room. He called out: “Ka‘b!” He said: “At your service, Messenger of Allah.” He said: “Reduce this debt of yours by this much,” and gestured to him, meaning half. He said: “I have done so, Messenger of Allah.” He said: “Get up and repay him.”

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, delivered an address and said: “Allah gave a servant the choice between this world and what is with Him, and he chose what is with Allah.” Abu Bakr, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, wept. I said to myself: “What makes this old man weep if Allah gave a servant the choice between this world and what is with Him, and he chose what is with Allah?” The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was that servant, and Abu Bakr was the most knowledgeable of us. He said: “Abu Bakr, do not weep. The person most generous to me with his companionship and wealth is Abu Bakr. If I were to take a close friend from my community, I would take Abu Bakr. But there is the brotherhood of Islam and its affection. Let no door in the mosque remain without being closed, except the door of Abu Bakr.”

arabic_blocks: [455] حدثنا عبد الله بن محمد الجعفي قال: حدثنا وهب بن جرير قال: حدثنا أبي قال: سمعت يعلى بن حكيم عن عكرمة عن ابن عباس قال خرج رسول الله ﷺ في مرضه الذي مات فيه عاصبا رأسه بخرقة فقعد على المنبر فحمد الله وأثنى عليه، ثم قال إنه ليس من الناس أحد أمن علي في نفسه وماله من أبي بكر ابن أبي قحافة ولو كنت متخذا من الناس خليلا لاتخذت أبا بكر خليلا ولكن خلة الإسلام أفضل سدوا عني كل خوخة في هذا المسجد غير خوخة أبي بكر

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came out during the illness in which he died, with a cloth wrapped around his head. He sat on the pulpit, praised Allah and extolled Him. Then he said: “No one has been more generous to me with himself and his wealth than Abu Bakr ibn Abi Quhafah. If I were to take a close friend from among the people, I would take Abu Bakr as a close friend. But the friendship of Islam is better. Close every small passage door in this mosque for me, except the small passage door of Abu Bakr.”

The women and children of the polytheists would stand watching him, amazed at him and looking at him. Abu Bakr was a man given to weeping; he could not control his eyes when he recited the Qur’an. arabic_blocks: [465] حدثنا مسدد قال: حدثنا أبو معاوية عن الأعمش عن أبي صالح عن أبي هريرة عن النبي ﷺ قال: صلاة الجميع تزيد على صلاته في بيته وصلاته في سوقه خمسا وعشرين درجة فإن أحدكم إذا توضأ فأحسن وأتى المسجد لا يريد إلا الصلاة لم يخط خطوة إلا رفعه الله بها درجة وحط عنه خطيئة حتى يدخل المسجد وإذا دخل المسجد كان في صلاة ما كانت تحبسه وتصلي يعني عليه الملائكة ما دام في مجلسه الذي يصلي فيه اللهم اغفر له اللهم ارحمه ما لم يحدث فيه
english_blocks: Musaddad related to us. He said: Abu Mu‘awiyah related to us, from al-A‘mash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

“Prayer in congregation exceeds his prayer in his house and his prayer in his market by twenty-five degrees. When one of you performs ablution well and comes to the mosque wanting only to pray, he takes no step without Allah raising him a degree by it and removing a sin from him, until he enters the mosque. When he enters the mosque, he is in prayer as long as it keeps him there. The angels pray—meaning, for him—as long as he is in the place where he prays: ‘Allah, forgive him. Allah, have mercy on him,’ as long as he does not break his state of ritual purity there.”

arabic_blocks: [466] حدثنا حامد بن عمر عن بشر حدثنا عاصم حدثنا واقد عن أبيه عن ابن عمر أو بن عمرو شبك النبي ﷺ أصابعه، وقال عاصم بن علي حدثنا عاصم بن محمد سمعت هذا الحديث من أبي فلم أحفظه فقومه لي واقد عن أبيه قال: سمعت أبي وهو يقول: قال عبد الله قال رسول الله ﷺ: يا عبد الله بن عمرو كيف بك إذا بقيت في حثالة من الناس بهذا
english_blocks: Hamid ibn ‘Umar related to us, from Bishr: ‘Asim related to us. Waqid related to us, from his father, from Ibn ‘Umar or Ibn ‘Amr:
The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, interlaced his fingers.

‘Asim ibn ‘Ali said: ‘Asim ibn Muhammad related to us: “I heard this report from my father, but I did not remember it. Waqid set it right for me, from his father.” He said: I heard my father saying: ‘Abd Allah said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:
“‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Amr, how will you be when you remain among the dregs of the people?”
With this.

arabic_blocks: [468] حدثنا إسحاق قال: حدثنا ابن شميل أخبرنا ابن عون عن ابن سيرين عن أبي هريرة قال صلى بنا رسول الله ﷺ إحدى صلاتي العشي قال ابن سيرين سماها أبو هريرة ولكن نسيت أنا قال: فصلى بنا ركعتين ثم سلم فقام إلى خشبة معروضة في المسجد فاتكأ عليها كأنه غضبان ووضع يده اليمنى على اليسرى وشبك بين أصابعه ووضع خده الأيمن على ظهر كفه اليسرى وخرجت السرعان من أبواب المسجد فقالوا قصرت الصلاة وفي القوم أبو بكر وعمر فهابا أن يكلماه وفي القوم رجل في يديه طول يقال له ذو اليدين قال: يا رسول الله أنسيت أم قصرت الصلاة قال لم أنس ولم تقصر، فقال أكما يقول ذو اليدين فقالوا نعم فتقدم فصلى ما ترك ثم سلم ثم كبر وسجد مثل سجوده أو أطول ثم رفع رأسه وكبر ثم كبر وسجد مثل سجوده أو أطول ثم رفع رأسه وكبر فربما سألوه ثم سلم فيقول نبئت أن عمران بن حصين قال ثم سلم
english_blocks: Ishaq related to us. He said: Ibn Shumayl related to us. Ibn ‘Awn informed us, from Ibn Sirin, from Abu Hurayrah, who said:
The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, led us in one of the two afternoon prayers.
Ibn Sirin said: Abu Hurayrah named it, but I forgot.

He said: He led us in two rak‘ahs and then gave the salam. He went to a piece of wood laid across the mosque and leaned against it as though he were angry. He placed his right hand over his left, interlaced his fingers, and put his right cheek on the back of his left palm. Those in a hurry left through the doors of the mosque and said: “The prayer has been shortened.” Abu Bakr and ‘Umar were among the people, but they were too awed to speak to him. Among the people was a man with long hands, called Dhu al-Yadayn. He said: “Messenger of Allah, have you forgotten, or has the prayer been shortened?” He said: “I have not forgotten, and it has not been shortened.” Then he said: “Is it as Dhu al-Yadayn says?” They said: “Yes.” He stepped forward and prayed what he had left, then gave the salam. Then he said the takbir and prostrated as he usually did, or longer. Then he raised his head and said the takbir. Then he said the takbir and prostrated as he usually did, or longer. Then he raised his head and said the takbir.
Sometimes they would ask him: “Then he gave the salam?” He would say: “I was informed that ‘Imran ibn Husayn said: ‘Then he gave the salam.’”

arabic_blocks: [469] حدثنا محمد بن أبي بكر المقدمي قال: حدثنا فضيل بن سليمان قال: حدثنا موسى بن عقبة قال: رأيت سالم بن عبد الله يتحرى أماكن من الطريق فيصلي فيها ويحدث أن أباه كان يصلي فيها وأنه رأى النبي ﷺ يصلي في تلك الأمكنة وحدثني نافع عن ابن عمر أنه كان يصلي في تلك الأمكنة وسألت سالما فلا أعلمه إلا وافق نافعا في الأمكنة كلها إلا أنهما اختلفا في مسجد بشرف الروحاء
english_blocks: Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr al-Muqaddami related to us. He said: Fudayl ibn Sulayman related to us. He said: Musa ibn ‘Uqbah related to us. He said:

I saw Salim ibn ‘Abd Allah seek out places along the road and pray in them. He related that his father used to pray in them and that he had seen the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, pray in those places.

And Nafi‘ related to me, from Ibn ‘Umar, that he used to pray in those places. I asked Salim, and I know of nothing other than his agreement with Nafi‘ about all the places, except that they differed about a mosque at Sharaf al-Rawha’.

arabic_blocks: [470] حدثنا إبراهيم بن المنذر قال: حدثنا أنس بن عياض قال: حدثنا موسى بن عقبة عن نافع أن عبد الله أخبره أن رسول الله ﷺ كان ينزل بذي الحليفة حين يعتمر وفي حجته حين حج تحت سمرة في موضع المسجد الذي بذي الحليفة وكان إذا رجع من غزو كان في تلك الطريق أو حج أو عمرة هبط من بطن واد فإذا ظهر من بطن واد أناخ بالبطحاء التي على شفير الوادي الشرقية فعرس ثم حتى يصبح ليس عند المسجد الذي بحجارة ولا على الأكمة التي عليها المسجد كان ثم خليج يصلي عبد الله عنده في بطنه كثب كان رسول الله ﷺ ثم يصلي فدحا السيل فيه بالبطحاء حتى دفن ذلك المكان الذي كان عبد الله يصلي فيه وأن عبد الله بن عمر حدثه أن النبي ﷺ صلى حيث المسجد الصغير الذي دون المسجد الذي بشرف الروحاء وقد كان عبد الله يعلم المكان الذي كان صلى فيه النبي ﷺ يقول: ثم عن يمينك حين تقوم في المسجد تصلي وذلك المسجد على حافة الطريق اليمنى وأنت ذاهب إلى مكة بينه وبين المسجد الأكبر رمية بحجر أو نحو ذلك وأن بن عمر كان يصلي إلى العرق الذي عند منصرف الروحاء وذلك العرق انتهاء طرفه على حافة الطريق دون المسجد الذي بينه وبين المنصرف وأنت ذاهب إلى مكة وقد ابتني ثم مسجد فلم يكن عبد الله يصلي في ذلك المسجد كان يتركه عن يساره ووراءه ويصلي أمامه إلى العرق نفسه وكان عبد الله يروح من الروحاء فلا يصلي الظهر حتى يأتي ذلك المكان فيصلي فيه الظهر وإذا أقبل من مكة فإن مر به قبل الصبح بساعة أو من آخر السحر عرس حتى يصلي بها الصبح وأن عبد الله حدثه أن النبي ﷺ كان ينزل تحت سرحة ضخمة دون الرويثة عن يمين الطريق ووجاه الطريق في مكان بطح سهل حتى يفضي من أكمة دوين بريد الرويثة بميلين وقد انكسر أعلاها فانثنى في جوفها وهي قائمة على ساق وفي ساقها كثب كثيرة وأن عبد الله بن عمر حدثه أن النبي ﷺ صلى في طرف تلعة من وراء العرج وأنت ذاهب إلى هضبة عند ذلك المسجد قبران أو ثلاثة على القبور رضم من حجارة عن يمين الطريق عند سلمات الطريق بين أولئك السلمات كان عبد الله يروح من العرج بعد أن تميل الشمس بالهاجرة فيصلي الظهر في ذلك المسجد وأن عبد الله بن عمر حدثه أن رسول الله ﷺ نزل عند سرحات عن يسار الطريق في مسيل دون هرشي ذلك المسيل لاصق بكراع هرشي بينه وبين الطريق قريب من غلوة وكان عبد الله يصلي إلى سرحة هي أقرب السرحات إلى الطريق وهي أطولهن وأن عبد الله بن عمر حدثه أن النبي ﷺ كان ينزل في المسيل الذي في أدنى مر الظهران قبل المدينة حين يهبط من الصفراوات ينزل في بطن ذلك المسيل عن يسار الطريق وأنت ذاهب إلى مكة ليس بين منزل رسول الله ﷺ وبين الطريق إلا رمية بحجر وأن عبد الله بن عمر حدثه أن النبي ﷺ كان ينزل بذي طوى ويبيت حتى يصبح يصلي الصبح حين يقدم مكة ومصلى رسول الله ﷺ ذلك على أكمة غليظة ليس في المسجد الذي بني ثم ولكن أسفل من ذلك على أكمة غليظة وأن عبد الله حدثه أن النبي ﷺ استقبل فرضتي الجبل الذي بينه وبين الجبل الطويل نحو الكعبة فجعل المسجد الذي بني ثم يسار المسجد بطرف الأكمة ومصلى النبي ﷺ أسفل منه على الأكمة السوداء تدع من الأكمة عشرة أذرع أو نحوها ثم تصلي مستقبل الفرضتين من الجبل الذي بينك وبين الكعبة
english_blocks: Ibrahim ibn al-Mundhir related to us. He said: Anas ibn ‘Iyad related to us. He said: Musa ibn ‘Uqbah related to us, from Nafi‘, that ‘Abd Allah informed him:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to stop at Dhu al-Hulayfah when performing ‘umrah, and on his Hajj when he performed Hajj, under a samurah tree at the site of the mosque at Dhu al-Hulayfah. When he returned from an expedition on that road, or from Hajj or ‘umrah, he descended into the valley bed. When he emerged from the valley bed, he made his camel kneel on the pebbly ground at the eastern edge of the valley and rested there until morning. It was not by the mosque built of stones, nor on the hill on which the mosque stood. There was a channel there, beside which ‘Abd Allah used to pray. In its bed were heaps of sand. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to pray there. Then the flood pushed pebbles into it until it buried the place where ‘Abd Allah used to pray.

And ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Umar related to him that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prayed where the small mosque stood, before the mosque at Sharaf al-Rawha’. ‘Abd Allah used to mark out the place where the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, had prayed, saying: “There, on your right when you stand in the mosque to pray.” That mosque was on the right edge of the road as you go toward Makkah. Between it and the larger mosque was a stone’s throw, or about that.

And Ibn ‘Umar used to pray toward al-‘Irq at Munsaraf al-Rawha’. The end of al-‘Irq reached the edge of the road, before the mosque between it and al-Munsaraf as you go toward Makkah. A mosque had been built there, but ‘Abd Allah did not pray in that mosque. He left it to his left and behind him, and prayed in front of it toward al-‘Irq itself. ‘Abd Allah used to leave al-Rawha’ and not pray Dhuhr until he reached that place, where he prayed Dhuhr. When coming from Makkah, if he passed it a while before dawn or at the end of the pre-dawn period, he rested until he prayed Subh there.

And ‘Abd Allah related to him that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to stop under a large sarhah tree before al-Ruwaythah, to the right of the road and facing the road, in a broad, level place, until he emerged from a hill two miles before the postal stop at al-Ruwaythah. Its top had broken and bent into its hollow. It remained standing on a trunk, with many heaps of sand at its base.

And ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Umar related to him that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prayed at the edge of a watercourse beyond al-‘Arj as you go toward a hill. Beside that mosque were two or three graves, with heaps of stones on the graves, to the right of the road by the roadside rocks. ‘Abd Allah used to leave al-‘Arj after the sun had declined in the midday heat and pray Dhuhr in that mosque among those rocks.

And ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Umar related to him that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, stopped by sarhah trees to the left of the road in a watercourse before Harsha. That watercourse adjoined the spur of Harsha, with about a bowshot between it and the road. ‘Abd Allah used to pray toward the sarhah tree nearest the road, which was the tallest of them.

And ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Umar related to him that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to stop in the watercourse at the nearest part of Marr al-Zahran toward Madinah when descending from al-Safrawat. He stopped in the bed of that watercourse, to the left of the road as you go toward Makkah. Between the stopping place of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and the road was only a stone’s throw.

And ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Umar related to him that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to stop at Dhu Tuwa and spend the night until morning, praying Subh when he came to Makkah. That prayer place of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was on a rough hill. It was not in the mosque built there, but lower down on a rough hill.

And ‘Abd Allah related to him that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, faced the two gaps in the mountain between him and the tall mountain toward the Ka‘bah. He placed the mosque built there to the left of the mosque at the edge of the hill. The prayer place of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was lower down on the black hill. Leave about ten cubits of the hill, or thereabouts, then pray facing the two gaps in the mountain between you and the Ka‘bah.

arabic_blocks: [471] حدثنا عبد الله بن يوسف قال: أخبرنا مالك عن ابن شهاب عن عبيد الله بن عبد الله بن عتبة عن عبد الله بن عباس أنه قال أقبلت راكبا على حمار أتان وأنا يومئذ قد ناهزت الاحتلام ورسول الله ﷺ يصلي بالناس بمنى إلى غير جدار فمررت بين يدي بعض الصف فنزلت وأرسلت الأتان ترتع ودخلت في الصف فلم ينكر ذلك علي أحد
english_blocks: ‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Ibn Shihab, from ‘Ubayd Allah ibn ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Utbah, from ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Abbas, who said:

I came riding a she-donkey when I was nearing puberty. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was leading the people in prayer at Mina without facing a wall. I passed in front of part of the row, dismounted, and let the donkey graze. I entered the row, and no one objected to me for that.

arabic_blocks: [472] حدثنا إسحاق قال: حدثنا عبد الله بن نمير قال: حدثنا عبيد الله عن نافع عن ابن عمر أن رسول الله ﷺ كان إذا خرج يوم العيد أمر بالحربة فتوضع بين يديه فيصلي إليها والناس وراءه وكان يفعل ذلك في السفر فمن ثم اتخذها الأمراء
english_blocks: Ishaq related to us. He said: ‘Abd Allah ibn Numayr related to us. He said: ‘Ubayd Allah related to us, from Nafi‘, from Ibn ‘Umar:

arabic_blocks: [491] حدثنا عبد الله بن يوسف قال: أخبرنا مالك عن أبي النضر مولى عمر بن عبيد الله عن أبي سلمة بن عبد الرحمن عن عائشة زوج النبي ﷺ أنها قالت كنت أنام بين يدي رسول الله ﷺ ورجلاي في قبلته فإذا سجد غمزني فقبضت رجلي فإذا قام بسطتهما قالت والبيوت يومئذ ليس فيها مصابيح

I used to sleep in front of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, with my legs in his qiblah. When he prostrated, he nudged me, and I drew my legs in. When he stood, I stretched them out.

english_blocks: Ahmad ibn Ishaq al-Surmari related to us. He said: ‘Ubayd Allah ibn Musa related to us. He said: Isra’il related to us, from Abu Ishaq, from ‘Amr ibn Maymun, from ‘Abd Allah, who said:

While the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was standing in prayer by the Ka‘bah, with a group of Quraysh in their gathering places, one of them said: “Do you not see this show-off? Which of you will go to the slaughtered camel of the family of so-and-so, take its stomach contents, blood and afterbirth, bring them, and wait until he prostrates, then place them between his shoulders?” The most wretched of them rose. When the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prostrated, he placed it between his shoulders. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, remained prostrating. They laughed until they leaned against one another with laughter. Someone went to Fatimah, peace be upon her, who was a young girl. She came running, and the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, remained prostrating until she threw it off him. She turned toward them, reviling them. When the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, finished the prayer, he said: “O Allah, deal with Quraysh. O Allah, deal with Quraysh. O Allah, deal with Quraysh.” Then he named them: “O Allah, deal with ‘Amr ibn Hisham, ‘Utbah ibn Rabi‘ah, Shaybah ibn Rabi‘ah, al-Walid ibn ‘Utbah, Umayyah ibn Khalaf, ‘Uqbah ibn Abi Mu‘ayt and ‘Umarah ibn al-Walid.”
‘Abd Allah said: By Allah, I saw them lying dead on the day of Badr. Then they were dragged to the well—the well of Badr.
Then the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “And the people of the well were followed by a curse.”
